data.summary: ddflow_claim with as_agent (a subagent sharing its parent's MCP connection) adopts the CONNECTION's harness worktree via adopt_existing, binding the subagent's item to the parent session's tree and branch: B-local-config-surfaces (agent local-config-surfaces) is bound to the parent's .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_015Nbh... on worktree-bridge-cse_015Nbh..., and the next subagent's ddflow_claim (contest-gaps, B-fix-contest-gaps) is refused 'this worktree is already bound to B-local-config-surfaces'. A claim under an as_agent identity different from the connection's should create its own tree (as the CLI from the primary does), not adopt the caller's. Workaround used: ddflow --agent contest-gaps claim from the primary checkout.

Lease contest OVER-report (safe direction, pre-existing): when a late renewal proves a displaced claim was live at its takeover, _late_renewal also joins the lease displayed at that moment into the contest whether or not it overlapped anyone (test_divergence _three_hops: carol [6000,7800] is contested though only alice/bob overlapped). The displayed lease stays in the contest after it is itself displaced. Kept deliberately in B-fix-contest-gaps because removing it makes `resolve --keep <current holder>` impossible: resolve refuses a keep that is the displayed lease but not a contestant. Fix both together (needs ddflow/api/items.py): let resolve keep the displayed lease, then join only pairwise overlaps.

(2) Found and fixed in the same change a fourth fold-order gap: a renewal of the DISPLAYED lease was never re-weighed against the record (test_a_renewal_of_the_displayed_lease_is_weighed_against_the_record fails on main and on the mutant). (3) Real logs folded with main vs this branch: ddflow (5365 events), run_nemo_run (13401), home-simulator (724) -> identical, no item contested or displaced either way, so doctor does not newly fail anywhere. Noted, not changed: an old-format release (holder only, no event) picks the holder's latest claim in displaced first -- with a same-holder record that can drop the older claim; such releases predate B191 and the claim was never on record before this change, so no regression. Also filed B7c7a0d9222 (ddflow_claim via as_agent adopts the parent's harness worktree).

The inline `known` list in _h_lease_acquired became _known(it), now shared by acquire, _late_renewal and the displayed-lease renewal path (one definition of "every claim the item knows"). _widen is the single place a renewal widens recorded copies of a claim; _join keeps its own max(renewed_at) merge for claims arriving with later evidence. Overlap is still only _overlaps/_clashing. Tests reuse the module's _ev/_acq/_holders helpers; the new history generator is the only one with per-holder sequencing.

data.summary: Pre-existing on main (b6a424a), found triaging the DeepSeek critic on B-fix-contest-gaps: a late renewal of a TTL-displaced claim joins its displacer `by` unconditionally, even after `by` was released. Fold h1 0+10, h2 15+10 (displaces h1), release h2 by event, then h1 renewal at 8 -> lease_contest [h1, h2] naming the RELEASED claim, with no displayed lease; the same events with the renewal folded before the release give no contest. Fold-order dependent, and violates the overjoin invariants (no released claim anywhere; a standing contest displays a claim).

data.claim: (1) false: _clashing excludes same-holder claims; (2) true as a behaviour change but main's behaviour was the bug: it revived a released claim into a contest with no displayed lease, and only when the release folded first (filed+fixed B-late-renewal-revives-release); (3) false by design: a holder id is one clone's, so a renewal at 14 after its own re-claim at 12 renews the re-claim (main attributes it the same way)
data.falsifier: the reviewers' folds produce a contest naming same-holder claims only (1), or a contest between unreleased claims missing (2), or a renewal from H's clone that cannot belong to H's latest claim (3)

data.rule: When a fold decides overlaps from remembered state, every path that replaces, renews or caps that state must keep the old claim reachable: a branch that just overwrites (same-holder re-claim), a cap that drops the oldest, or a lookup that searches one list of two each silently hides a real conflict. Write the invariant as a property over random histories with every event kind interleaved in every per-writer-consistent order, and run it against the unfixed code first.
data.title: A fold's 'what the item still knows' must include every claim, not just the ones a branch happened to keep
